question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's set $u=\log{\left(\frac{x^{3}}{125} \right)}.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3}{x}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $5$ | $5 e$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $3$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{25}\int_{5}^{5 e}\frac{4\operatorname{ln}({\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}^{3})}{5\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{8}{125}\int_{5}^{5 e}\operatorname{ln}({\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}^{3})\cdot \frac{1}{\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{8}{25}\int_{0}^{3}u\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{8}{75}\int_{0}^{3}u\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(\frac{4}{15}\cdot {\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}}\right)|_{0}^{3} \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(\frac{4}{15}\cdot \frac{9}{2}\right) \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(\frac{6}{5}\right)\end{aligned}
$$
